title: Unhandled Promise Rejection and Missing Await in Auth
platform_conditions: Node.js runtime (Promises/A+ semantics, async/await); identical semantics in browsers for client-side guards
security_mechanism: Calling an async function returns a Promise; forgetting await means the Promise<boolean> object itself is truthy, so if (!checkAuth(req)) is always false and the request proceeds regardless of the eventual result. The rejection, when it comes, is unhandled: in modern Node it crashes the process (unhandledRejection default) or, with a handler attached, silently drops the decision. The same gap yields check-then-act races across await -- state can change between the check and the guarded operation -- and swallowed rejections (.catch(() => {}) or missing catch in a helper) turn failed authorization into fail-open.

source_sink_clues.source: Request-scoped authentication/authorization calls and any async guard function whose result gates a sensitive operation.
source_sink_clues.sink: async guard invoked without await in a conditional; floating Promises before sensitive operations; empty .catch handlers on auth paths; check-then-act sequences spanning an await

tracking_guards: Check every security-decision call is awaited inside the conditional; check linters/no-floating-promises enforcement; check catch paths fail closed (deny) rather than return the success branch; check authorization is re-verified after any await that crosses a mutation of the guarded resource.
not_candidate_when: The call is intentionally fire-and-forget with no security decision downstream and rejections are explicitly handled, the guarded operation is re-authorized after the await, or the function is synchronous so no Promise is involved.
public_references: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html
